---
title: "check-visualization-figures.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, blocking check that flags a div that asks for a picture
but has no figure.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-26) is that every div whose title mentions
visualization (visualize, visualizing, visualization) has a corresponding
figure, and that for an exercise the solution includes it.
The trigger is wider than that one word,
so the rule's own example, "Mark every zero-gradient point on a surface",
is caught.
A div asks for a picture when

- its title, for an exercise or example, has a visual word:
  `visuali[sz]*`, plot, sketch, draw, contour, picture, diagram,
  or "mark" with point, curve, surface or region;
- its title, for a definition, theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary or remark,
  has `visuali[sz]*`
  (a definition of a plot type gets its figure from the example that follows it);
- its prompt, for an exercise, says sketch or visualize,
  or plot as a verb, or draw a dendrogram, tree, diagram, picture, figure,
  graph, contour, curve or line, outside its code fences.

Words that name something else, such as graph, "draw a sample"
and "draw conclusions", do not trigger it.
A div's title is its `title="..."` attribute or the text of its first heading.
A `#fig-` or `#sol-` div is the figure or the answer itself,
never the subject.

A figure is anything `check-exm-figures` counts:

- a Markdown image or an `<img>` tag;
- a div or chunk labelled `fig-`
  (`{#fig-...}`, `#| label: fig-...`, `#| fig-cap:` or `#| fig-alt:`);
- a cross-reference to a figure (`@fig-...`);
- an include of a figure subfile (`{{< include ..._fig.qmd >}}`).

For an exercise, the figure may also be in

- a `#sol-<slug>` div in the same file, where `<slug>` is the exercise's id
  without its `exr-` prefix, or
- another file of the same exercise family in the same folder:
  `_exr-a.qmd`, `_sol-a.qmd`, `_exr-a-part2.qmd` and `_sol-a-part2.qmd`
  share the base name `a`, since a multi-part exercise shows its figure once.

A false positive or a justified exception carries a reason:
an HTML comment `<!-- no-figure: reason -->` inside the div exempts it.
Use `paths-ignore` to exempt whole paths.

## Scope

Only a div that holds a line a pull request adds is reported,
so existing divs are never reflagged.
A changed solution file puts its exercise family in scope too,
since removing the solution's figure leaves the exercise without one.
With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file on purpose.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default       | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd'`     | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`          | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `true`        | Fail the workflow when a visualization div has no figure. Set `false` for warning annotations only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`       | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`      | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | `'ubuntu-latest'` | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on the runner ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-visualization-figures.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a div that asks for a picture (visualize, plot, sketch, ...)
# but has no figure (an exercise may have it in its solution) when a PR adds a line to it.
# Add a figure, or <!-- no-figure: reason --> in the div.
# Blocking by default.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check visualization figures

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-visualization-figures.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd'                        # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'   # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                             # set false to warn only (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                       # scan every file, not just a PR's additions
```

See
[`examples/check-visualization-figures.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-visualization-figures.yml)
for the full caller stub.
